purpose: Selectable and earned character collections, component recipes, applied-asset review and deeper game planning across four families.

prompts.intent: Organize stable character identities, interchangeable recipes and collection scope.
reference_requirements: Existing roster/format or explicit absence, approved family briefs and intended game/theme/level contexts.
prompts.prompt: Author a character collection from {{CURRENT_COLLECTION}}, {{FAMILY_BRIEFS}} and {{TARGET_CONTEXTS}}. Separate stable character identity, cosmetic variant, source/derivative artwork, replaceable component recipe, context eligibility, acquisition rule and current selection. Preserve existing IDs when replacing an image or propeller treatment. Give each character a coherent reason to exist beyond a palette swap, while keeping movement, collider, capture, damage and scoring unchanged unless the user explicitly requests a separately reviewed rules change. Retain the four independent families: Ukrainian FPV equipment, specific Ukrainian cultural characters, wider 80s–90s nostalgia and Coupa-inspired business characters. Record body, portrait, rotor/wing/thruster/pulse and trail references only where useful and supported. Inspect the actual preview format before writing records; the collection is not automatically a content-pack or media-schema extension. Deliver a concise roster and recipe mapping with starter/earned intent, fallback choices and readiness evidence. Mark new images, unsupported selectors and unimplemented progression as planned rather than inventing working outputs.
prompts.example_request: Create a roster with starter and earned characters across all four themes, preserving the existing character IDs.

prompts.intent: Create distinct compact FPV bodies while preserving Ukrainian identity and attachment structure.
reference_requirements: Actual inspected FPV body, requested chassis/finish differences and intended play-size fixture.
prompts.prompt: Inspect {{SOURCE_AVATAR}} before creating the requested {{VARIANT_DIRECTION}} for {{DISPLAY_TARGET}}. Produce a separately saved FPV body derivative with a practical compact frame, camera/battery structure, a readable central core and restrained Ukrainian blue/yellow identification. Use no Z markings anywhere, and keep Ukrainian player identity explicit rather than borrowing hostile military markings. Preserve the source and its parent reference, the accepted north-facing view, body center and intended rotor-hub positions unless the requested variant deliberately changes a documented anchor. Keep rotor blades independently replaceable when the preview supplies them; do not bake extra spinning blades or a giant glow into the body. Distinguish a racer-looking or night-looking cosmetic from actual speed or stealth abilities. Compare occupied pixels at the target scale without changing the collider or level geometry. Use the built-in image-edit route with the inspected reference, record the effective prompt and actual dimensions, and label the result as a concept until alpha, fit, anchor placement and applied playback are reviewed.
prompts.example_request: Create racer and night FPV body cosmetics from the accepted body, without granting extra speed or stealth.

prompts.intent: Specify configurable three-blade propellers with honest phase, anchor and aliasing behavior.
reference_requirements: Actual body/hub reference, blade/rate preferences and supported renderer recipe fields.
prompts.prompt: Use {{COMPONENT_REFERENCE}}, {{ROTOR_PREFERENCES}} and {{PREVIEW_FORMAT}} to prepare a configurable FPV propeller recipe. Distinguish four rotor hubs from three blades at each hub: hub count and blade count are different parameters. Keep three blade silhouettes evenly spaced around each inspected hub, with separately recorded radius, local anchor, spin sign, phase offset and visual rate. Read the actual preview implementation before choosing field names and accepted bounds; unsupported options remain a proposal. Let the body, blades, trail and decorative effects be exchanged independently while preserving gameplay position, speed and collider. Define phase continuity during normal rate changes, deliberate phase handling on character exchange, pause and reduced-motion steady views, and cleanup of old rotors. At high rates inspect temporal aliasing, apparent reversal and tiny-size noise rather than claiming realistic RPM. Use an appropriate simpler blur/ring treatment when supported. Deliver the recipe and concrete playback cases at slow, normal and boost states; a drawn propeller sheet alone does not verify motion.
prompts.example_request: Make the FPV quadcopter use three blades per propeller, with configurable phase and visual speed.

prompts.intent: Create a cultural character with identifiable material and separable motion parts.
reference_requirements: A specific researched Ukrainian chapter or material tradition, original character brief and intended visual size.
prompts.prompt: Create one original UKRAINE ATLAS character using {{CHAPTER_REFERENCE}}, {{CHARACTER_BRIEF}} and {{DISPLAY_TARGET}}. Keep its regional or material identity specific: a swallow-shaped painted charm, carved falcon or thread bird can belong to different researched chapters rather than one indiscriminate folklore mixture. Translate the selected reference into a memorable small silhouette with a clear central player marker. Where the brief calls for motion, make body and wing/ornament boundaries readable for later independent assembly; do not imply that a static generated sheet already supplies clean alpha or an animation rig. Preserve generous visual breathing room around the active trail and use the chapter palette without forcing neon. Cultural figures, traditions and peoples are not enemy identities. This is a selectable cosmetic character, not a source of new movement or capture abilities. Record references, full effective prompt, output dimensions and source status. Review the actual image and prepare its component/collection handoff; do not claim exact museum authenticity, production export or applied preview without evidence.
prompts.example_request: Create a Ukrainian swallow starter and a separate carved-falcon earned look, each with a coherent material identity.

prompts.intent: Create an original nostalgic craft without making every variant neon.
reference_requirements: Chosen 80s/90s direction, original craft brief and actual play-size target.
prompts.prompt: Create an original 1994 FOREVER character from {{ERA_DIRECTION}}, {{CHARACTER_BRIEF}} and {{DISPLAY_TARGET}}. Choose a clear nostalgic vocabulary such as a home-computer cursor craft, toy-like space skimmer or restrained vector-era ship; do not mix all decades into generic neon. Give the character a readable tiny silhouette, an unambiguous forward direction and a bright functional center that can lead the live cut. Keep body and intended thruster/accent boundaries suitable for later independent replacement; no exhaust or glow should cover the next turn. Design the selectable or earned variant as a cosmetic identity, preserving the baseline collider, movement and capture rules. Use original forms rather than tracing recognizable commercial game sprites. Keep functional labels outside generated art. Record the effective prompt, selected references and measured output dimensions, and inspect the resulting image at its intended scale. A beautiful keyframe is a concept until alpha, sampling, attachments and actual applied motion have been checked in the available preview.
prompts.example_request: Create a warm home-computer starter craft and an earned vector-style cosmetic with the same movement rules.

prompts.intent: Adapt approved business character identity into a selectable cosmetic variant.
reference_requirements: Actual inspected approved identity or explicitly labeled original placeholder, character variation brief and display target.
prompts.prompt: Inspect {{IDENTITY_REFERENCE}} and create the requested NAVI NETWORK variation described by {{CHARACTER_BRIEF}} for {{DISPLAY_TARGET}}. Preserve the supplied identity accurately; if it is an original C-token or unverified mascot concept, retain that label and do not claim an exact official Coupa Navi reproduction. Keep the character friendly, compact and readable, with an independently replaceable pulse/accent or connection cue where supported. A starter guide and an earned auditor-themed cosmetic can differ in silhouette detail or material without implying real customer savings, changed speed or new AI capability. Keep process-friction obstacles abstract and introduce no military imagery or nationality-coded enemies. Preserve the original source, save a derived copy and record the complete prompt and parent asset. Generated labels should not replace actual localized UI. Inspect real output dimensions, alpha and small-size clarity, then apply the asset through the existing preview only when that step is requested and available. Report concept, applied visual and inspected motion readiness separately.
prompts.example_request: Adapt the supplied Navi placeholder into an earned auditor look, retaining honest brand status and business imagery.

prompts.intent: Apply a real replacement through the current recipe and verify the visible switch.
reference_requirements: Actual target recipe, accessible replacement file with provenance and current preview documentation.
prompts.prompt: Apply {{REPLACEMENT_ASSET}} to the requested component in {{TARGET_RECIPE}} using the actual capabilities in {{PREVIEW_CAPABILITIES}}. Inspect both source and target before changing a binding. Preserve original bytes and stable character identity, record the derivative parent and effective prompt when the replacement was generated, and modify only the supported visual reference or component fields. Keep body, portrait, propeller/wing/thruster/pulse and trail independently replaceable where the renderer supports them. Do not copy the replacement's apparent size into collider or movement data. After applying, verify successful file loading and inspect the painted result rather than trusting a filename or network response alone. Check proportional fit, alpha, heading, occupied pixels, anchors and the absence of the old component. Switch away and back, including while paused, and confirm labels and visuals agree. Report actual changed paths, tested scenarios and unsupported work. This execution prompt authorizes no imaginary asset, external upload, paid generation fallback or full game implementation. Preserve the authored immediate or grid-center buffered turning mode through the exchange. Compare swaps within both supported modes against their own movement baselines, using current preview documentation for exact semantics.
prompts.example_request: Apply this new three-blade/body asset recipe, switch to another character and back, and inspect the actual result.

prompts.intent: Define eligible selection and explicit fallback across supported contexts.
reference_requirements: Actual collection format, context cases and explicitly simulated or real progress provenance.
prompts.prompt: Review {{COLLECTION_DATA}}, {{CONTEXT_CASES}} and {{PROGRESS_FIXTURE}} to define context-aware character selection. Use only selectors accepted by the actual format; the current lab names gameId, themeId, caseId, challengeId, levelId and mapId, with omitted selectors unrestricted within a scope. Read composition and matching behavior from the current implementation rather than inventing precedence. Distinguish requested selection, unlocked status, context eligibility, applied character and asset-loaded status. Cover a starter with no progress, an earned eligible character, a locked request, family/context changes, a missing asset and a previously selected character becoming unavailable. Choose an explicit eligible fallback and explain it in UI; do not silently equip a wrong-family or locked character. Cosmetic context changes must preserve geometry, movement, fill and stats. Keep simulated fixtures clearly separate from production saves. Deliver a decision table and data edits only in supported fields, with ambiguous or unsupported policies recorded as design questions instead of hidden assumptions. Context or character selection must preserve the independently configured immediate or grid-center buffered turning policy. Do not store it as an unsupported collection selector or silently reset it to immediate movement.
prompts.example_request: Choose an eligible character for a case, challenge or level, with clear fallback when the previous choice is locked or out of context.

prompts.intent: Plan understandable cosmetic rewards with duplicate-safe simulated evidence.
reference_requirements: Requested progression, actual evaluator/collection data and accepted event-fixture fields.
prompts.prompt: Author earned-character rules from {{PROGRESSION_BRIEF}}, {{COLLECTION_DATA}} and {{EVENT_FIXTURES}}. Keep starter access, cosmetic rewards, current selection and file readiness distinct. Explain each reward through understandable completion or optional mastery conditions rather than unexplained scarcity. Use the actual evaluator's supported condition types and selectors; do not introduce arbitrary expressions or game code into a collection recipe. Count distinct accepted level identities for clear totals and use best per-level stars where that is the documented behavior, so replaying the same easy fixture cannot repeatedly farm credit. Test both a qualifying and a failing result, duplicate/replayed events and context changes. Every lab event remains explicitly simulated and belongs to the preview profile, not a real player save, leaderboard or analytics pipeline. No fixture proves the unimplemented game emits that event. Mode flags segregate preview and game namespaces but do not authenticate locally rewritten data; never reflag a fixture as production, and record a trusted result/save adapter as a future dependency. Deliver exact condition IDs, expected eligibility/unlock outcomes and remaining production decisions. Keep changes to stats, abilities or challenge difficulty in a separately reviewed rules/balance proposal.
prompts.example_request: Preview earned racer, falcon, retro and auditor cosmetics using labeled simulated clears, without replay-grind inflation.

prompts.intent: Design focusable selection, preview, equip and reward states across devices.
reference_requirements: Actual/proposed UI flow, collection status fields and input/device targets.
prompts.prompt: Design character collection UI for {{UI_FLOW}}, {{COLLECTION_DATA}} and {{INPUT_TARGETS}}. Make preview, equip, selected, starter, earned, locked, unavailable-in-context, missing-art and loading/error states distinguishable. Use real localized labels outside generated images and preserve focus/scroll when returning from a character preview. A locked item may be inspectable without becoming equipped or changing progress. Show an understandable condition and current eligible scope; keep simulated reward controls visibly separate from ordinary collection actions. Keyboard/controller focus must have a shape or contrast cue, and touch needs an intentional selection/equip action rather than hover. Keep the small active avatar visible for immediate comparison without forcing a whole screen of particle effects. Record how context changes choose and explain a fallback and how rapid switching cancels old components. Preserve the fixed arena and gameplay state. Deliver state transitions and review cases, marking native-device behavior untested until actual input/hardware evidence exists.
prompts.example_request: Let players preview, select and understand how to earn characters on desktop and phone without confusing preview with equip.

prompts.intent: Inspect character swaps in a shared fixture with exact evidence limits.
reference_requirements: Actual applied file/recipe inventory, unchanged board/motion fixture and available playback evidence.
prompts.prompt: Inspect {{APPLIED_ASSETS}} in {{SHARED_FIXTURE}} using {{PREVIEW_EVIDENCE}}. Confirm that the requested character IDs actually paint the intended source files and component recipes, then compare at normal and narrow browser viewport sizes. Check the occupied body/attachment envelope, visible core, heading, alpha, trail origin and whether rotor or wing details hide the next turn. Compare compact/microtile, detailed-object and hybrid terrain over identical geometry and motion. Exercise supported idle, movement, turn, slow, boost, pause/resume and rapid character exchange; verify stale propellers, pulses, labels or effects do not survive the switch. Inspect three-blade motion for sample-rate aliasing and non-rotor parts for appropriate family behavior. Missing assets must be labeled, not promoted by a neutral fallback. Record the exact files, IDs, sizes and scenarios reviewed. A browser viewport is not an iPhone emulator, and this preview does not certify game collision, progression, controller latency, production sprite quality or frame-rate performance on unavailable hardware. Record and test both configured turning modes, immediate and grid-center buffered, when supported. Compare cosmetics within each mode against its own matched baseline; do not require identical paths across the two policies. Take queue, release, reversal and mode-switch semantics from the current preview documentation.
prompts.example_request: Compare every applied character on the same route and all three terrain styles, including paused switching and small viewport readability.

prompts.intent: Separate data, media, application, motion and unlock evidence.
reference_requirements: Actual collection/preset files, source/derivative records and concrete review/test outputs.
prompts.prompt: Review {{COLLECTION_OUTPUTS}}, {{REGISTERED_MEDIA}} and {{PREVIEW_EVIDENCE}} without collapsing their readiness into one badge. Check stable IDs, supported selectors, unlock references, source paths, parent provenance and declared asset status against the actual separate collection/media formats. Inspect real images for identity, dimensions, alpha, proportional fit and source preservation. Then verify applied selection and component playback only in scenarios for which a running preview and evidence exist. Separate cosmetic recipe validation, manually inspected visuals, played animation, simulated reward evaluation and game-runtime integration. A valid record with a planned image is still planned; an image loaded from disk is not automatically reviewed; a passed simulated unlock is not production progression. Mode flags do not authenticate edited saves or result payloads; a production guarantee requires trusted game-result ingestion rather than relabeling fixtures. Confirm explicit fallback when an eligible character lacks artwork and preserve progress identity through a visual replacement. Report concrete defects with file locations, actual commands or clips examined, and the smallest remaining proof. Do not claim a complete set because every roster slot has a name or contact-sheet thumbnail. Include cosmetic-independence evidence for both supported immediate and grid-center buffered turning modes. Preserve the selected policy and record missing mode coverage honestly; a changed path between policies is not itself a cosmetic defect.
prompts.example_request: Audit which characters have real applied art, working motion and tested simulated unlocks, and which remain planned.

prompts.intent: Keep cosmetic collections distinct from explicitly requested gameplay classes.
reference_requirements: Requested character differences, actual baseline rules and current balance assumptions.
prompts.prompt: Evaluate {{REQUESTED_VARIANTS}} against {{BASELINE_RULES}} and {{BALANCE_QUESTIONS}}. Classify each difference as identity/art, component animation, eligibility/progression or an actual gameplay change. A racer shell, large falcon wing, thruster glow or auditor badge remains cosmetic unless the user explicitly requested distinct speed, collider, damage, abilities or capture behavior. Preserve the approved baseline when authoring collection records. If gameplay classes are desired, describe a separate opt-in rules/balance proposal with clear capability dependencies, comparison metrics and implications for fair challenges or leaderboards. Do not encode unrecognized stats into the current collection or content pack to make that proposal look implemented. Discuss how a late-game cosmetic remains desirable through style, discovery and mastery recognition rather than assumed power. Separate historical reference observations from retention hypotheses. Deliver a concise decision table, unresolved design choices and a bounded validation plan; do not start game logic or silently widen the task while reviewing character variety. Treat immediate versus grid-center buffered turning as an independent authored movement option. Preserve the user's configurable choice rather than attaching it to an earned skin, inferring it from visual body response or normalizing every test to immediate turns.
prompts.example_request: Decide which character differences should stay cosmetic and what a future optional gameplay-class mode would require.

prompts.intent: Review the deeper game plan before expanding game logic.
reference_requirements: Current game-design plan, collection direction and actual status of authoring/preview/game features.
prompts.prompt: Review {{GAMEPLAY_PLAN}}, {{COLLECTION_PROPOSAL}} and {{IMPLEMENTED_CAPABILITIES}} before implementing more game logic. Check that the first playable loop has explicit movement, live-cut failure, fill policy, enemy domains, terrain meanings, capture quota, life loss/respawn, timer purpose, rewards and gallery/retry flow. Integrate selectable and earned characters as a clear cosmetic layer with stable context selection and truthful asset readiness. Retain four coherent families and compact/microtile, detailed-object and hybrid appearance modes without multiplying rule engines. Distinguish observed Xposed/Xonix reference behavior from our proposals and identify which unsupported behaviors require versioned extensions. Prioritize the smallest playable proof and the questions it should answer about control, clarity, fairness and voluntary replay. Keep browser authoring tools, simulated progression and generated concepts separate from implemented game features. Deliver concrete gaps, sequencing and acceptance evidence, with only material remaining choices for discussion. This review must not create game runtime code or present a plan as tested fun. Retain both user-requested configurable turning policies, immediate and grid-center buffered, in the plan and comparison criteria. Read the current demo's exact semantics before specifying queue, release, reversal or alignment behavior; test cosmetic independence against a separate baseline for each policy.
prompts.example_request: Review the whole game plan and character collection before we start implementing capture and enemy logic.

prompts.intent: Specify wings, thrusters and pulses as distinct replaceable motion recipes.
reference_requirements: Actual character/attachment references, desired supported component kinds and available state signals.
prompts.prompt: Design {{COMPONENT_TYPES}} for {{CHARACTER_REFERENCES}} using {{STATE_INTERFACE}}. Treat a cultural bird wing, retro thruster and business-character pulse as different motion systems, not rotor animations with renamed labels. Define inspected local hinges/nozzles/centers, transform ownership, bounds, draw order, idle/move responses and reduced-motion steady views. A wing can use bounded angular motion, a thruster can change length or opacity, and a pulse can vary a restrained accent only where the actual renderer supports those fields. All response reads declared state and velocity without altering authoritative movement or collider geometry. Specify loop/timebase, pause/resume behavior, priority and cancellation on supported hit/respawn/victory or character exchange. If the avatar art already contains wings or exhaust, explain how overlays avoid duplicated anatomy and clipping. Keep original media and stable character/component IDs. Deliver the recipe and an actual playback checklist; unsupported controls and unplayed motion remain explicitly proposed, and no sound exists merely because a cue is described. Preserve the configured immediate or grid-center buffered movement policy. Derive response from documented actual travel/state signals, which may differ from a requested buffered direction; compare each cosmetic recipe within both supported mode baselines without changing turn logic.
prompts.example_request: Give the Ukrainian bird wings, retro craft a thruster and Navi a quiet pulse, with independent recipes and clean character switching.

prompts.intent: Create a style derivative without losing accepted character or collection identity.
reference_requirements: Inspected accepted character image, requested style change and explicit locked composition/anchors.
prompts.prompt: Inspect {{SOURCE_ART}} and create only the requested {{STYLE_VARIATION}} while respecting {{COMPONENT_LOCKS}}. Preserve the original file, stable collection identity, subject, heading, center and accepted attachment relationships unless the user explicitly requested a change. Keep-source with a separate overlay remains valid; do not automatically pixelate a painting or photographic source. For a requested derived style, save a separate asset with its parent, effective prompt and actual dimensions. Keep skin detail independent from gameplay speed, collider, capture and earned state. Respect the active family: no Z markings on current FPV variants, specific Ukrainian cultural references, coherent 80s–90s vocabulary and correctly labeled Coupa/Navi identity without military imports. Use the built-in image-edit route with inspected references. Compare the result under an unchanged live-trail fixture and at the intended occupied-pixel scale. Report fidelity differences and inspect alpha/anchors before application; a completed style edit does not by itself prove a working animated or production-ready character.
prompts.example_request: Create pixel, painterly or clean illustrated looks for the same accepted character while preserving its collection ID and anchors.
